arXiv:math/9906129v1 [math.AG] 18 Jun 1999

Algebraic Gauss-Manin Systems and Brieskorn Modules

Alexandru Dimca and Morihiko Saito
Abstract

We study the algebraic Gauss-Manin system and the algebraic Brieskorn module associated to a polynomial mapping with isolated singularities. Since the algebraic Gauss-Manin system does not contain any information on the cohomology of singular fibers, we construct a non quasi-coherent sheaf which gives the cohomology of every fiber. Then we study the algebraic Brieskorn module by comparing it with the Deligne extension, and show that its pole part is determined by the vanishing cycles at infinity. In the two-dimensional case we describe the algebraic Gauss-Manin system explicitly.

Keywords: 
Gauss-Manin system, Brieskorn lattice, D{D}-module, perverse sheaf, vanishing cycle
Classification: 
32S40

Introduction

Let f:X→Sf:X\rightarrow S be a morphism of smooth complex algebraic varieties. The Gauss-Manin systems Gfi{G}_{f}^{i} of ff are defined to be the (cohomological) direct images of OX{O}_{X} as algebraic left D{D}-Modules. They are regular holonomic DS{D}_{S}-Modules, and correspond by the de Rham functor DR to the (perverse) higher direct images of the constant sheaf. In particular, they give the cohomology with compact support of each fiber, but not the cohomology of singular fibers unless ff is proper, because the stalk of the higher direct image does not coincide with the cohomology of the fiber due to the vanishing cycles at infinity. Furthermore the cohomologies of the fibers do not form a constructible sheaf in a natural way, and it is not easy to construct a quasi-coherent sheaf on SS which is generically coherent, and contains the information on the cohomology of every fiber.

In §1, we study the algebraic Gauss-Manin system and the filtration on it, and prove (0.1-3) in a more general situation. In §2, we apply the theory of perverse sheaves [3] to the study of the higher direct image sheaves of the constant sheaf, and generalize some results in [1], etc. The notion of cohomological isolated singularity including at infinity is introduced in §3. The two-dimensional case is studied in §4, and we prove (0.8).

Convention. In this paper, algebraic variety means a separated scheme of finite type over ℂ{\mathbb{C}}. For a variety XX and a morphism ff, we denote ℂXan{\mathbb{C}}_{X^{\text{\rm an}}} by ℂX{\mathbb{C}}_{X}, and fanf^{\text{\rm an}} by ff to simplify the notation, where XanX^{\text{\rm an}} is the associated analytic space. Similarly, Hi​(X,ℂ)H^{i}(X,{\mathbb{C}}) and Hci​(X,ℂ){H}_{c}^{i}(X,{\mathbb{C}}) denote respectively Hi​(Xan,ℂ)H^{i}(X^{\text{\rm an}},{\mathbb{C}}) and Hci​(Xan,ℂ){H}_{c}^{i}(X^{\text{\rm an}},{\mathbb{C}}). A point of a variety means always a closed point, and x∈Xx\in X means x∈X⁡(ℂ)x\in X({\mathbb{C}}).

We denote the nearby and vanishing cycle functors [10] by ψ\psi, φ\varphi, and ψ⁡[−1]\psi[-1], φ⁡[−1]\varphi[-1] by ψp{}^{p}\psi, φp{}^{p}\varphi, because they preserve perverse sheaves.

1. Gauss-Manin Systems and Filtration

1.1. Let f:X→Sf:X\rightarrow S be a morphism of smooth algebraic varieties. Let n=dimXn=\dim X. We assume in this paper dimS=1\dim S=1, ff is not constant and X,SX,S are connected.
